original_question: Suppose f in End(C^n,O) has expansion f(z)=z+P_nu(z)+O(||z||^{nu+1}) and all characteristic directions are non-degenerate. Is f topologically locally conjugated to the time-1 map of the homogeneous vector field P_nu?
target_in_paper: Section 3.5, OP15: the open problem asking whether a tangent-to-the-identity germ with only non-degenerate characteristic directions is topologically locally conjugated to the time-1 map of its leading homogeneous vector field.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact statement. It correctly identifies the ambient class f ∈ End(C^n,O), the tangent-to-the-identity expansion f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+O(||z||^{ν+1}), the hypothesis that all characteristic directions are non-degenerate, and the precise target model: the time-1 map of the homogeneous vector field P_ν. This is essentially OP15 rewritten in your own words.
missing_details: State explicitly that f is a holomorphic germ over C: End(C^n,O) means germs of holomorphic self-maps of C^n fixing O.
Make explicit that ν ≥ 2 and that P_ν is the first nonzero term in the convergent homogeneous expansion of f, i.e. f is tangent to the identity of multiplicity ν.
Specify that P_ν is an n-tuple of homogeneous polynomials of degree ν, viewed as a homogeneous holomorphic vector field on C^n.
Define characteristic direction: a nonzero vector v ∈ C^n \ {O} such that P_ν(v)=λv for some λ ∈ C; equivalently one may speak of the associated projective direction [v] ∈ P^{n-1}(C).
Define non-degenerate characteristic direction: λ ≠ 0, equivalently P_ν(v) ≠ 0; degenerate means λ = 0.
Clarify that the comparison map is the local time-1 map g of the ODE dot z = P_ν(z).
Clarify the meaning of topologically locally conjugated: there should exist neighborhoods of O and a homeomorphism fixing O that conjugates f to g locally.
If one wants the genuinely open content isolated, note that the n=1 case is already known by Corollary 1, so the substantive unknown case is in several variables.
refined_question: Let f ∈ End(C^n,O) be a holomorphic germ tangent to the identity of multiplicity ν ≥ 2, with convergent homogeneous expansion f(z)=z+P_ν(z)+O(||z||^{ν+1}), where P_ν=(P_{ν,1},…,P_{ν,n}) is the first nonzero term and each P_{ν,j} is a homogeneous polynomial of degree ν. Assume that every characteristic direction of f, meaning every nonzero v ∈ C^n with P_ν(v)=λv for some λ ∈ C, is non-degenerate in the sense that λ ≠ 0. If g denotes the local time-1 map of the homogeneous holomorphic vector field dot z=P_ν(z), must f be topologically locally conjugated to g near O?
justification: The draft is targeting OP15 exactly, not a neighboring broader problem. Section 3.4 sets up the notation for tangent-to-the-identity germs and defines characteristic directions. Section 3.5 then introduces time-1 maps of homogeneous vector fields, states the one-dimensional motivating result in Corollary 1, and formulates OP15 in essentially the same words as your draft. The sentence immediately after OP15 explains why the non-degeneracy assumption is necessary. The nearby Theorem 16 gives formal-classification context for germs with non-degenerate characteristic directions, but it is not an equivalent reformulation of OP15, so there is no paper-explicit alternate formulation to report.
